Combine mayonnaise, Parmesan cheese, Cheddar cheese, jalapeños, and green chilies in a bowl.
Slice off the top of the sourdough round and hollow out the center to create a sturdy bread bowl. Fill the bread bowl with the jalapeño mixture.
Bake in the preheated oven until heated through and golden on top, about 30 minutes.

raw_recipe.headline: Insanely Amazing Jalapeño Cheese Dip
raw_recipe.description: This jalapeño cheese dip made with Cheddar, Parmesan cheese, mayonnaise, green chiles, and canned jalapeño peppers is baked in a sourdough bread bowl.

video.description: You’ll be the crowd-pleaser when you please with the power of cheese in this crazy-good spicy dip! Grab yourself a round loaf of sourdough, slice off its top and hollow out the center to make a serving bowl. Then fill it to the brim with an incredible mixture of fresh jalapeno peppers, Parmesan cheese, Cheddar cheese, mayonnaise and green chilis. Bake until gloriously melted, then place into the center of a slumber party, sports weekend gathering or a potluck that needs a bit of a pick-me-up! Serve with chips, crackers or toasted bread.

Combine mayonnaise, Parmesan cheese, Cheddar cheese, jalapeños, and green chilies in a bowl.

Bake in the preheated oven until heated through and golden on top, about 30 minutes.

review.reviewBody: I am the submitter of this recipe. 1.) Make sure to use real cheese, as the powdered stuff in the green can has a lot more sodium, and will cause the dip to be salty! 2.)If you don't like spicy, or if a lot of kids will be eating this, I would use about 2 oz. of jalapenos. If you like a little kick but not overpoweringly spicy, 4 oz is the way to go. If you can't get enough of the heat and like almost-inedibly spicy, you can try 6 oz. 3.) The best thing I have found to dip in this is sliced french or sourdough baguette. 4.)Also, if you want to use fresh jalapenos, it gives a wonderful texture. Enjoy!!!

Three stars as is but five stars with some easy changes. Having made this recipe several times before, I recommend the following changes/ additions: Substitutie 1 ( 8 oz) package of soft cream cheese, and 1/4 cup of sour cream to replace mayo (mayo is too sweet and sour cream adds a needed tang), bake this in a greased casserole dish instead of a bread bowl and then serve with toasted french baguettes (dough wont get soggy then and dip forms a golden brown layer on top). Divide the parmasen cheese into two half cups. Incorporate one 1/2 cup with the cream cheese mixture and save the other 1/2 cup for a topping (also my addition). Mix 1/4 tsp garlic powder, salt and pepper to taste into cream cheese and sour cream mixture. For the topping, combine 3/4 cup Italian bread crumbs, the 2nd 1/2 cup of parmesan, 4 TBS melted butter and salt and pepper to taste. Once you have transferred the dip to the baking dish, spread the bread crumb mixture evenly over the top. Bake uncovered in a 350 oven for 30 minutes (or until the top is bubbly and golden brown). Serve with toasted baguettes. I would highly recommend doubling this recipe for a crowd. I always run out even after doubling and literally have people licking the bowl. SO GOOD! Thanks!

On my 3rd revision of this recipe now. So far I've ditched baking it in the bread bowl in favor of a shallow casserole dish then transferring to a browned sourdough bowl. Also since I have no taste buds left I have upped the pepper count to 6 roasted, peeled & chopped jalapeños, 2 fresh chopped jalapeños & 2 roasted, peeled & chopped Poblano peppers along with 2-3 cloves minced garlic, 1/4 cup grated yellow onion (patted dry between paper towells) & 1/4 cup chopped green onions. For the truly ambitious, substitute 1-2 Habanero peppers. I also substitute 1/2 cup sour cream OR Greek yogurt for the mayo, nix the Parmesan cheese in favor of a 1/2 cup jack & "almost" a full 8oz. log of softened cream cheese & then add about a 1/4 cup of panko crumbs to to mixture to offset the additional moisture from the fresh peppers & onions & just bind everything together. I also find that panko crumbs, a few tablespoons of Durkee fried onions, dry jack cheese ( & yes, some cayenne pepper) quickly toasted with butter makes a really tasty topping.

I ended up making this in a dish Instead of putting in a bread bowl, and I made a Jalapeño cheddar sourdough loaf to serve with it... INCREDIBLE. I'm not usually a Jalapeño person but I could not stop eating it. My family said I have to make it for every occasion going forward, and I'm really looking forward to the next family get together. 100/10 recipe. And trust me, I was skeptical. Thank you

This was a huge hit at the Library Volunteers Luncheon.
Everyone wants the recipe. I’m giving it four stars only because I made changes. Besides the cheddar, I found “smoky bacon cheddar” which I think added another flavor, and I used fresh as well as canned jalapeños. I also omitted the mayonnaise for the cream cheese and sour cream another reviewer suggested as well as adding a topping of Italian bread crumbs, melted butter and grated Parmesan. I also made the mixture the day before so it would have a more intense flavor.
Definitely will make again and again!

I also put In 1 cup of sour cream, and use fresh jalapeños. I don't always put chilies in. Huge hit at potluck, everyone asks me to bring this dip. Definitely rip the bread bowl apart at the end. Mmmm.

I substituted 1 ( 8 oz) package of soft cream cheese, and 1/4 cup of sour cream to replace mayo. I baked this in a cake pan instead of a bread bowl and then served with toasted french baguettes. It was good but I would add more spice to it next time by adding freshly slice jalapeno in addition to the canned.

Great recipe. I didn't use the bread bowl. Just put in the oven until hot and bubbly. First I topped it with 1 cup of crushed crackers mixed with 4 oz. of melted butter and 1/2 cup of parmesan cheese. Served with crackers. Everyone loved it.

I took the advice of omitting the mayo and subbing 8 oz cream cheese and 1/4 C sour cream. I also chopped 1 large jalapeno instead of using canned and added 1/4 tsp garlic powder. For the topping, I omitted the butter and just used panko bread crumbs and grated parmesan. Couldn't get enough of this dip. I served it with sliced celery and baby carrots. Chips are always good too.

I'm giving this 5 stars for as good as it is, for as simple as it is - all premade ingredients, comes together in no time at all. And it IS good! I used 4-5 oz of jarred, pre-diced jalapeno with seeds, and it WAS spicy! It reminds me of a deconstructed jalapeno popper. I used half mayo, half sour cream just because that's what I had; worked well. I served it in a tiny crockpot to keep it warm, which worked out well (can't say if it stays yummy as it cools). I wasn't sure about the untoasted bread dippers, so I buttered and toasted half of the baguette slices, took it to a party with both options, and polled the audience -- split vote: some preferred toasted, while others liked the plain bread. So either way works!

Thank you Happywife!! This dip was the hit of the party. I pretty much followed the recipe but didn't have quite a cup of mayo so I added enough sour cream (per reviewers) to make a cup. I used fresh jalapenos because I had them but I think the canned ones probably would have added more heat. I baked this first in a casserole dish and did notice some grease on top but once I transferred to the bread bowl you didn't see it as the bread soaked it up. I think the cheeses more than the mayo cause the little bit of grease. The only thing I'd do differently next time would be to triple it!

My boss handed down this recipe for me to make at company functions after he retired. He made it every pot luck. I then lost it lol. When I went searching and found this, thank the lord! It’s a dead ringer. I usually don’t do the bread bowl though, I burn bread on the regular… it just is what it is… and after pulling it out at one party with 2 ft flames… I just stick with putting it in a casserole dish now! Though it did liven up the party!

I somewhat follow this recipe. I occasionally add sour cream or cream cream in addition to the mayonnaise. I generally add additional cheese and sometimes do not add jalapenos or less than a full can, depends on how much spice I want. I also use pumpernickel instead of sour dough if the bakery is out. Overall it's a great dip that is very versatile.
One of the best dips I have ever had. Everyone loved it. Has a kick, so if you don't like super spicy, cut back on the diced jalapenos. :)
Blended exactly as written, using one finely chopped fresh jalapeño. Microwaved 2.5 minutes, and this was the best chip dip ever! We skipped the bread.

The recipe title says it all. This is excellent! Amazingly enough it wasn't overly spicy which is a good thing for most people. If you are hosting a party I recommend making a double batch because it most definitely will not last long. I will be making this often. I think it would be be good cold and not baked too.

I've been making this for years and it's Awesome! It's not the healthiest recipe but everyone loves it and it always goes. Usually people are ripping apart the bread bowl to get every bit of it. It is spicy especially if you make it ahead of time (longer it sits in frig the spicier it gets). So the only change I make is to use less jalapeños peppers. The chili peppers are not spicy so I always use the full amount. That is just my personal taste, my son loves spicy food and likes the recipe as is.
Don't use grated parm. Shredded is better.

So good and easy to make! I didn't have any canned jalapenos but our garden had tons of fresh ones so I made it with entirely fresh jalapenos (equivalent weight of about 4-5 ounces) and I used fresh bell peppers from the garden as well instead of the other canned peppers. I also went with the recommended 1/2 sour cream 1/2 mayo. It was a little drier looking than the video but it came out delicious! Enjoyed on ciabatta bread.
A 5 star with changes that reviewer used. I used 1/2 cup cream cheese and 1/2 sour cream instead of mayo. It was delicious!!
